title: OSPFv2 DR and BDR Elections
summary: Configure and verify OSPFv2 Designated Router (DR) and Backup Designated Router (BDR) election mechanics on multi-access broadcast networks using interface priorities.
learning_objectives: Explain the necessity and operational role of DR and BDR routers in multi-access broadcast OSPF networks
Examine default OSPF election criteria based on priority, manual router ID, and highest active IP address
Configure custom OSPF interface priorities using the ip ospf priority command to deterministically designate DR and BDR routers
Prevent a multi-access router from ever participating in elections by configuring priority 0 (DROTHER state)
Verify OSPF adjacency states (FULL/DR, FULL/BDR, FULL/DROTHER) and timer intervals across multi-access interfaces
Demonstrate deterministic DR failover when the primary DR becomes unavailable
Verify the non-preemptive nature of OSPF elections when higher priority routers rejoin an established network

source.origin: Independently authored enterprise multi-access OSPFv2 curriculum guide aligned with Cisco CCNA exam topic 3.2
